MarketDataPoint.description:
Single OHLCV data point.

The four trailing fields (``session_type``, ``quality_score``,
``source_count``, ``data_quality``) are populated from
``analytics.market_data`` and surfaced to the frontend chart so it can
render the quality strip, session bands and tooltip qualité. They are
optional because historical rows ingested before the ingestion pipeline
started populating them may carry ``NULL``. ``data_quality`` is typed as
``str`` rather than a strict ``Literal`` because the DB enum
(``raw|validated|reconciled|official_eod|estimated|interpolated|corrected|aggregated``)
is the source of truth and we forward it verbatim (no transformation) —
the frontend already accepts ``string | null`` here.

ask.description: Last observed ask in the candle's bucket — same NULL semantics as ``bid``.
ask.title: Ask

bid.description: Last observed bid in the candle's bucket (migration 141). NULL for OHLCV-only sources (Yahoo/Polygon/Stooq/EOD/backfill/gap-fill) and for historical rows ingested before this column was tracked. Never split/spinoff-adjusted (NULL when ``adjusted=true``).
bid.title: Bid

quality_score.description: 0-100 quality score from the ingestion pipeline
quality_score.title: Quality Score

source_count.description: Number of distinct sources that contributed to this candle
source_count.title: Source Count

volume_unit.description: Unit of the ``volume`` field — 'shares' when the broker reports real trade volume, 'ticks' when the candle uses the tick-count proxy, 'last_size' for last-size based feeds (IB/Alpaca/Yahoo WS), 'quote_notional' for quote-currency notional feeds (e.g. Binance USDT = price×qty). NULL for legacy rows ingested before this column was tracked.
volume_unit.title: Volume Unit

PortfolioDetailResponse.description:
Enhanced portfolio detail with positions, allocations, and P&L.

Unit split, deliberate and load-bearing: the ``total_*`` aggregates are in
the **portfolio's** currency (FX-converted per position via
``app.portfolio.calculators.realized_pnl``), while the ``realized_pnl`` /
``unrealized_pnl`` carried by each :class:`PositionResponse` in
``positions`` are raw, i.e. in that **symbol's** currency. Summing the
latter client-side does NOT reproduce the former on a cross-currency book.
PortfolioDetailResponse.title: PortfolioDetailResponse

PortfolioResponse.description:
Full portfolio detail returned from the API.

``allocation_mode`` was removed on 2026-05-17 (Wave 3): the DB column
survives for legacy seeds but the strategy engine reads the runtime
sizing mode from ``trading.composite_strategies.allocation_mode``
(``app/strategy/consumer/base.py:1352``). The frontend used to badge
the value on PortfolioCard / PortfolioHeader / settings, which was
misleading — the badge now reads the per-strategy allocation_mode
instead.
PortfolioResponse.title: PortfolioResponse

PortfolioStrategyLink.description: Represents a link between a portfolio and a strategy.
PortfolioStrategyLink.title: PortfolioStrategyLink

PositionResponse.description:
Full position detail.

Unit: ``average_price``, ``last_price``, ``market_value``,
``unrealized_pnl`` and ``realized_pnl`` are all in the **symbol's**
currency, straight from ``portfolio.positions``. That is unambiguous for a
single position and it is what a per-position display should show — but it
means these fields must NOT be summed across positions without conversion.
Use the pre-aggregated ``total_*`` fields of
:class:`PortfolioDetailResponse`, or
``app.portfolio.calculators.realized_pnl``.

``symbol_currency`` names that unit so a reader no longer has to guess it
(the guess used to be the portfolio's currency, which prints "250 €" next
to a share that trades at $250). ``None`` means
``reference.symbols.currency_code`` is NULL for this instrument — a data
hole, not a licence to substitute a default.
PositionResponse.title: PositionResponse

post.description: Refresh access token using refresh token from httpOnly cookie.

Generate a JWT token for WebSocket authentication.

The token lifetime is controlled by ``ws_token_ttl_seconds`` (defaults
to the access token TTL when set to 0).  It includes the
``type=websocket`` claim so that the WebSocket handshake can
distinguish it from regular access tokens.

The frontend refreshes the WS token proactively before expiry and
sends the new token over the existing connection via a
``refresh_token`` message, avoiding reconnection.

Send a command to an edge device.

Requires JWT authentication. The device must belong to the authenticated
user (or user must be admin).

The command is enqueued in the device's Redis command queue. The device
retrieves it via GET /commands or SSE.

post.description:
Register or update an Android device FCM token for the authenticated user.

The token is stored per device (identified by ``device_fingerprint``).
Calling this endpoint again with the same fingerprint updates the token
(upsert), which handles the case where FCM rotates the registration token.

NOTE: This endpoint commits directly via ``repo.session.commit()`` rather
than delegating to a service layer.  This is a known pattern exception
for this simple single-statement upsert — adding a service method would
be pure boilerplate with no business logic to encapsulate.

get.description: Get enhanced portfolio detail with positions, allocations, and P&L.

Get performance metrics for a portfolio over the requested window.

``period='all'`` (default) returns inception-to-date metrics. The other
windows recompute Sharpe / Sortino / volatility / max-drawdown /
total-return on the windowed daily-snapshot equity curve, and
win-rate / profit-factor on trades closed within the window. An
out-of-set value is rejected with HTTP 422 by the ``pattern`` above.

Get PNL summary for a portfolio over a given period.

P&L numerics (realized / unrealized / total) reflect the **lifetime
cumulative** state of the portfolio, sourced directly from
``portfolio.positions``:

* ``realized_pnl`` — Σ ``realized_pnl`` across every position ever
  opened (active + closed). The column is updated atomically by
  ``PositionRepository.update_position_fifo`` SELL path with the
  true FIFO P&L per close event.
* ``unrealized_pnl`` — Σ ``unrealized_pnl`` across currently-active
  positions only. Recomputed live by
  ``update_position_price_atomic`` from ``last_price``.
* ``total_pnl`` — sum of the two; matches
  ``current_value - initial_capital`` to within rounding.

Both columns are stored in the **symbol's** currency, so both sums are
FX-converted into the portfolio's currency via
``app.portfolio.calculators.realized_pnl`` — the same factor
``current_value`` itself is built with. Until 2026-07-26 this endpoint
summed them raw and labelled the result with the portfolio currency: on
the production ``test`` book (EUR, 30 USD positions) that reported
-627.33 € for an actual -551.40 €, a 75.93 € overstatement of the loss.

The previous implementation summed raw BUY costs vs SELL proceeds in
the period without FIFO matching, treating every fresh entry as a
"loss" (no cost-basis offset). That produced phantom losses equal to
the period's BUY total for any portfolio actively opening positions
— e.g. a -5870.55 € display for an actually -141.96 € portfolio.

The ``period`` parameter still scopes ``trades_count`` /
``winning_trades`` / ``losing_trades`` to recent activity. The P&L
numerics are period-independent because reconstructing per-period
realized P&L correctly requires either FIFO replay or a snapshot
diff path (the latter is a follow-up once
``portfolio.portfolio_value_history.daily_pnl`` is populated).

get.description:
Return the circuit-breaker status for a single portfolio.

Reflects the violation counter that ``RiskManager._check_circuit_breaker``
reads at proposal-validation time (Redis key
``circuit_breaker:{portfolio_id}``). The state is derived by comparing the
counter to the active rule's ``max_violations``:

* ``state="closed"`` — count below threshold (or no rule active).
* ``state="open"``   — count at or above threshold; the validation
  pipeline is currently rejecting proposals for this portfolio.

Mirrors the validation pipeline's fail-closed policy when Redis is
unreachable: the response sets ``redis_unavailable=true`` and
``state="open"``.
